questions.q: Which of these are characteristics used to compare storage devices? Tick all that apply.
questions.feedback: Six characteristics. Clock speed belongs to a processor and colour depth to an image.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 4 — Top Trumps, station 1: The six characteristics

questions.q: State what is meant by the capacity of a storage device.

markPoints.concept: how much data it can hold
markPoints.exemplar: How much data it can hold.

questions.example: How much data the device can hold, usually measured in gigabytes or terabytes.
questions.paraphrase: The amount of data it is able to store.
questions.feedback: Capacity is quantity. Speed is how quickly that data can be reached.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 4 — Top Trumps, station 1: The six characteristics

questions.q: Match each characteristic to what it means.
pairs: How well it survives being knocked or dropped
How easily it can be carried about
How likely it is to keep working over a long time
questions.feedback: Durability is about shocks, reliability is about time, portability is about size and weight.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 4 — Top Trumps, station 1: The six characteristics

questions.q: Sort each statement by which storage type it describes best.
items: Cheapest per gigabyte for very large capacities
Cheap to produce in huge numbers for distributing films
Most easily damaged by being dropped while running
questions.feedback: Magnetic for capacity and cost, solid state for speed and durability, optical for cheap distribution.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 4 — Top Trumps, station 5: Head to head

questions.q: A photographer needs to carry 2 TB of photographs between studios every day. Justify a suitable storage device.

markPoints.concept: names a portable drive of sufficient capacity
explains that it has the capacity needed
markPoints.exemplar: It has enough capacity to hold 2 TB.

markPoints.concept: justifies the choice against the daily carrying
accept: no moving parts|nothing moving|nothing moves|nothing inside to break
durable|robust|survive|withstand|cope with|stand up to|less likely to be damaged|will not break
markPoints.exemplar: An SSD has no moving parts, so it survives being carried about every day.

questions.example: A portable external SSD. It can be bought with well over 2 TB of capacity, and because it has no moving parts it will survive being carried between studios every day far better than a portable hard disk would.
questions.paraphrase: I would choose an external solid state drive: they come in sizes above two terabytes, and because nothing moves inside one it will cope with being transported daily.
questions.feedback: A justification names the device, checks it meets the requirement, and says why it beats the alternative.
